section_summary: This section covers the disputed purge of Jiichiro Matsumoto, Prime Minister Shigeru Yoshida’s appeal for support of Japan’s recovery, and reports on Communist Party strategy and Professor Ikuo Oyama. It also contains lists of political prisoners released after the war and repeated copies of an intelligence article standardizing terminology for the Japan Communist Party.

subfiles.title: Memorandum on Tokyo despatch 243 and Matsumoto’s purge
subfiles.about: The Soviet member of the Allied Council protests Jiichiro Matsumoto’s purge.
subfiles.summary: Notes Soviet support for Matsumoto and possible Communist Party outreach to the outcaste community.

subfiles.title: Soviet Protest Against Purge of Matsumoto Jiichiro
subfiles.about: Transmits the Soviet member’s protest against Matsumoto’s disqualification.
subfiles.summary: Reports broad Japanese opposition to the purge and observes that Allied headquarters has not intervened.

subfiles.title: Soviet member’s letter protesting Matsumoto purge
subfiles.about: Requests cancellation of Jiichiro Matsumoto’s political disqualification.
subfiles.summary: Argues that Matsumoto’s purge is unjust and contrasts it with the rehabilitation of men the writer associates with Japanese militarism.

subfiles.title: Prime Minister’s Address at Tokyo Correspondents Club
subfiles.about: Transmits and comments on Yoshida’s May 11 address.
subfiles.summary: Explains Yoshida’s rejection of the labels “reactionary” and “die-hard” and his appeal for international help with Japan’s economic recovery.

subfiles.title: Address of the Prime Minister at the First Annual Prime Minister’s Dinner
subfiles.about: Yoshida appeals for international understanding and access to materials and markets.
subfiles.summary: Yoshida thanks foreign correspondents and Allied authorities for their role in Japan’s recovery. He rejects descriptions of his party as reactionary, recalls opposition to wartime militarists, and says Japan seeks peaceful trade, food, and self-support under its recovery program.

subfiles.title: Memorandum on Tokyo despatch 265 and Communist Party strategy
subfiles.about: Summarizes new struggle principles announced by the Japan Communist Party.
subfiles.summary: Notes popular-front aims, attacks on economic stabilization, and concern about a shift toward forceful revolution.

subfiles.title: Oyama Ikuo
subfiles.about: Transmits a memorandum on Professor Ikuo Oyama’s return to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Identifies the attached account as the recollection of a former military intelligence officer.

subfiles.title: Memorandum on Oyama Ikuo
subfiles.about: Reviews Oyama’s political associations and the circumstances of his 1947 return to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Traces interest in Oyama among Japanese and American leftists, Professor Colegrove, and General Whitney. Spinks says the precise arrangements for Oyama’s return remain unclear and suggests consulting Army Department files.

subfiles.title: Political prisoners released from Japanese prisons
subfiles.about: Sends two lists of political prisoners released at the end of the war.
subfiles.summary: Explains gaps in 1945 records and the different sources of the enclosed lists.

subfiles.title: Political Prisoners Released after the War
subfiles.about: Lists released prisoners by name and place of confinement.
subfiles.summary: A long tabular enclosure identifies prisoners held under the Justice, Navy, and War ministries. Page 265 and part of page 266 repeat the same opening entries. The list records detention sites throughout Japan but generally gives no political affiliation.

subfiles.title: Political Prisoners Released by Directive, 4 October 1945
subfiles.about: Lists prisoners released by directive and their stated or suspected political affiliations.
subfiles.summary: Names detainees identified as Communists, Socialists, labor activists, liberal professors, or suspected sympathizers.

subfiles.title: Japan Communist Party Organizational Terminology
subfiles.about: Transmits copies of a military intelligence article on Communist Party terminology.
subfiles.summary: Emphasizes the need for consistent English translations of Japanese party terms.

subfiles.title: Japan Communist Party Organizational Terminology, first copy
subfiles.about: Defines the Japan Communist Party’s organizational structure and terminology.
subfiles.summary: Sets out party echelons from the National Congress to cells, distinguishing fractions from factions. It defines position titles, headquarters bodies, publications, directives, and national through district meetings, arguing that standardized translation will improve intelligence reports.

subfiles.title: Japan Communist Party Organizational Terminology, second copy
subfiles.about: Repeats the article defining Japan Communist Party organizational terminology.
subfiles.summary: A second copy covers the same seven sections: hierarchy, titles, departments, publications, meetings, and the need for standardized terminology.

subfiles.title: Japan Communist Party Organizational Terminology, third copy
subfiles.about: Begins another copy of the article on Japan Communist Party terminology.
subfiles.summary: Repeats the introduction and descriptions of the party hierarchy, cells, fractions, and position titles; this copy continues beyond page 302.
